notes: Almond, shaqed, sounds like watching, shoqed. The wordplay explains the vision’s connection to the LORD’s word.
vocabulary: These agricultural verbs frame the commission alongside demolition and building; they recur through Jeremiah.

notes: Verse 20 retains the written “I will not serve”; the recorded reading has “I will not transgress.” The opening “I broke” in verse 20 can also be understood as an older form of “you broke.” Verse 34 uses an older second-person feminine form, “you found them.” The accusation concerns innocent poor people killed without a break-in defense.
The head-grazing image can suggest shaving or devastation. The wild donkey’s sexual behavior is part of the poem’s accusation, not a description of women in general.
vocabulary: Fresh, flowing water from a spring, contrasted with stored water in a cracked cistern.

sections.1: A people who abandoned their spring

notes: “Return to me” in verse 1 can be a question or a command. Verse 14’s “husband” can also mean master; the marriage image continues alongside the address to children.
vocabulary: A contemptuous designation for an object of worship, associated here with the loss of animals and children.

notes: The prophet directly accuses God of deception in verse 10; the draft does not reassign those words. Verse 19 follows the recorded “you have heard,” addressed to the speaker’s own soul.
vocabulary: Tohu wa-vohu echoes Genesis 1:2. The following loss of light, people, birds and fruitful land portrays creation coming undone.

notes: Verse 10’s vine rows can also be understood as walls. Verse 28’s prospering may describe the orphan’s successful case or the wrongdoers’ prosperity. Verse 31 may describe priests acting under the prophets’ direction or by their own authority.
vocabulary: The same verb links serving foreign gods at home with serving foreigners in exile.

sections.20: A people who will not listen

notes: The difficult verb in verse 2 can mean destroying or comparing. Verse 7’s well image can mean keeping water fresh or making it flow. Verse 27 retains “fortress” beside “assayer”; another interpretation reads “ore.”
vocabulary: Shalom includes safety and well-being. Its repetition here is a false assurance, contradicted by the untreated fracture.

notes: “Let you live” can also be read “dwell with you.” The command to eat burnt offerings is deliberately jarring. The following denial concerning sacrifice is retained without adding “merely” or “primarily” to reconcile it with other texts.
Sons and daughters are explicitly burned. The LORD rejects both commanding and conceiving this practice; the valley is then renamed for the coming slaughter.
vocabulary: A refuge used by violent robbers; the accusation concerns treating the temple as shelter while continuing wrongdoing.
